Bangladesh begins Family Card data drive, targeting 44.5 million households by December
Share
Copy Link
A national register with a much smaller first payment list
Bangladesh has begun collecting household information nationwide for its Family Card programme, with Social Welfare Minister AZM Zahid Hossain setting a target of entering an estimated 44.5 million families into a database by December 2026.
The government plans to give cards and allowances to 4 million new female household heads during the 2026–27 financial year, selecting recipients from that larger register.
Contents
The household definition will shape the register
10. Key Points
The exercise began on Monday, October 12, with 66,815 data collectors and 6,681 supervisors assigned to the work.
The government has allocated Tk145 billion, or Tk14,500 crore, to the programme for the current financial year. Of that, Tk123 billion is reserved for allowances.
Why the earlier database matters
The operation was renamed the Family Card Household Database after objections to its initial title, Family Card Census 2026.
Advertisement
The Social Welfare Ministry's October 8 letter said trained government personnel carrying official identity cards would visit households. The exercise follows the Family Card Thana Database Information Collection Guidelines, 2026, and asks families to give information reflecting their actual economic and social circumstances.
Officials mentioned a National ID card, photograph and active mobile number as likely requirements, with birth registration potentially available as an alternative to National ID. Those were proposed arrangements; the October exercise centres on household visits by authorised collectors.
Zahid said the estimate of 44.5 million families was calculated by treating every five people as one family. That is the planning basis for the national target. February proposals also specified one card per household to prevent duplicate benefits.
* Nationwide Family Card data collection began on October 12, 2026, with 66,815 collectors and 6,681 supervisors.
* Zahid set a target of 44.5 million household records by December; a November 30 collection target covered 35 million to 40 million households.
* The pilot recorded 112,094 families and provided cards and allowances to 71,831 eligible beneficiaries.
* The government aims to add 4 million female household heads to the programme in 2026–27.
* The annual allocation is Tk145 billion, including Tk123 billion for allowances.
* Beneficiaries will be selected using household information, automated software and PMT scores.
* Household information collection is free. Demands for money should be reported to 1098.

Bangladesh’s Family Card: A New Approach to Poverty Reduction
Bangladesh's Family Card Bangladesh’s family card program is a new government initiative launched on March 10, 2026, designed to provide direct financial assistance and essential goods to low-income households.
Developed by the Ministry of Social Welfare, the program is designed as a digital, database-driven system that identifies and supports vulnerable families through a single platform.
Unlike traditional welfare schemes that often focus on individuals, the government built this program on the principle that families are the core unit of development.
One of the key features of the family card program is its role in unifying Bangladesh’s social protection system. In the past, welfare support was often delivered through multiple programs across different ministries, leading to duplication, inefficiencies and gaps in coverage.
The program addresses this by integrating various forms of assistance, such as cash transfers and subsidized goods, into one system.
This centralized approach allows the government to maintain a single database of beneficiaries, improving coordination and ensuring that support reaches the intended households.
The family card program is designed to support economically vulnerable households across Bangladesh, particularly those with unstable incomes or limited access to basic resources. These include rural families, day laborers and households affected by rising living costs.
Bangladesh’s family card program reflects a broader shift toward digital governance and integrated social protection. By combining technology, centralized data and direct transfers, the initiative aims to create a more efficient and accessible support system.
